pageProps.title: The Depth
pageProps.review: Patrick Süskind's The Depth is a short story that provides a deep resonance to the reader by briefly and intensely insightfully examining the reality where 'depth', a social standard, encroaches on individual lives and the duality of standards one applies to oneself.
pageProps.content:
## Review A short story with no fluff. It's short but intense, impactful, and has deep resonance.
In the book, it's expressed as an artist and a critic, but this duality exists everywhere. It shows the reality where depth becomes a yardstick for measuring the depth of life, and ```social conditions``` gradually eat away at even individual lives.
This yardstick is also applied to oneself. It seems that the yardstick one applies can turn into development or into despair.
